pack.title: Science & Nature
pack.description: Small wonders, big ideas, and nature’s double meanings.

categories.title: PLANETS BEYOND EARTH
categories.triviaFact: Saturn is less dense than water when its mass is averaged over its entire volume.

categories.title: METALLIC ELEMENTS
categories.triviaFact: Mercury is a metal that remains liquid at ordinary room temperature.

categories.title: DECIDUOUS TREES
categories.triviaFact: Deciduous trees shed their leaves seasonally, reducing water loss during unfavorable conditions.

categories.title: BEFORE CELL
categories.triviaFact: A dry cell uses an electrolyte held in a paste rather than a freely flowing liquid.

redHerrings.note: MERCURY looks like a fifth planet, but it completes the four metallic elements and leaves four unambiguous planets.

categories.title: INSECTS
categories.triviaFact: Insects have three pairs of legs attached to their thorax.

categories.title: STATES OF MATTER
categories.triviaFact: Plasma contains charged particles and occurs naturally in lightning.

categories.title: UNITS NAMED AFTER SCIENTISTS
categories.triviaFact: A hertz measures one cycle per second, making it useful for describing frequency.

categories.title: BEFORE WAVE
categories.triviaFact: An electroencephalogram records electrical activity commonly described as brain waves.

redHerrings.note: SOUND goes naturally with HERTZ, but is not a measurement unit; its three partners all make familiar WAVE expressions.

categories.title: MINERALS
categories.triviaFact: Talc sits at the softest end of the Mohs scale of mineral hardness.

categories.title: CELL STRUCTURES
categories.triviaFact: Ribosomes assemble proteins by linking amino acids together.

categories.title: CLOUD WORDS
categories.triviaFact: Cirrus clouds are made mostly of ice crystals high in the atmosphere.

categories.title: BEFORE STONE
categories.triviaFact: A lodestone is naturally magnetized magnetite and can attract iron.

redHerrings.note: LIME suggests mineral chemistry, but SAND, TOUCH and LODE complete four familiar compounds ending in STONE.

categories.title: MOONS OF GIANT PLANETS
categories.triviaFact: Titan has a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid hydrocarbons on its surface.

categories.title: UNITS OF VOLUME
categories.triviaFact: The imperial gallon and the US gallon represent different volumes.

categories.title: OPTICAL COMPONENTS
categories.triviaFact: A prism separates white light because different wavelengths bend by different amounts.

categories.title: FOLLOW RAIN
categories.triviaFact: A rainbow forms when sunlight is refracted and reflected inside water droplets.

redHerrings.note: BOW suggests the rainbow colors that a PRISM produces, but BOW, COAT, DROP and FALL all follow RAIN.

categories.title: POLLINATING ANIMALS
categories.triviaFact: Some bats pollinate flowers while feeding on nectar.

categories.title: PARTS OF A FLOWER
categories.triviaFact: Sepals usually protect a flower while it is still a bud.

categories.title: COMPUTER HARDWARE
categories.triviaFact: A router directs data packets between networks.

categories.title: FOLLOW FIRE
categories.triviaFact: A firewall controls which network traffic may pass according to a set of rules.

redHerrings.note: MOUSE looks like another animal, but KEYBOARD, MONITOR and ROUTER give it a complete computing connection.

categories.title: SIMPLE MACHINES
categories.triviaFact: A screw converts turning motion into movement along its axis.

categories.title: PARTS OF AN ATOM
categories.triviaFact: Most of an atom's mass is concentrated in its central nucleus.

categories.title: GEOLOGICAL PROCESSES
categories.triviaFact: Subduction carries one tectonic plate beneath another.

categories.title: ALSO MEAN TO ACCUSE
categories.triviaFact: Indict means to formally accuse someone of a crime.

redHerrings.note: CHARGE suggests electrons and protons, but it is a property rather than an atomic part; the accusation verbs give it a home.

categories.title: ANIMAL COLLECTIVES
categories.triviaFact: A pod often describes a social group of dolphins or whales.

categories.title: PARTS OF A WAVE
categories.triviaFact: Wavelength measures the distance between matching points on successive waves.

categories.title: SCIENTISTS WITH ELEMENT NAMESAKES
categories.triviaFact: Curium honors both Marie and Pierre Curie for their work on radioactivity.

categories.title: BEFORE WORK
categories.triviaFact: Fieldwork gathers information in a real setting rather than only in a laboratory.

redHerrings.note: TEAM can name a group of draft animals alongside PRIDE or HERD, but FIELD, NET and FRAME need it for four WORK compounds.

categories.title: HEAT TRANSFER TERMS
categories.triviaFact: Advection carries heat along with the bulk movement of a fluid.

categories.title: DNA BASE NAMES
categories.triviaFact: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine and guanine pairs with cytosine.

categories.title: ANIMALS WITH MISLEADING NAMES
categories.triviaFact: Despite its name, a seahorse is a fish rather than a miniature land mammal.

categories.title: BOTH SCIENCE AND EVERYDAY VERBS
categories.triviaFact: Chemical bonds involve the interactions of electrons between atoms.

redHerrings.note: DECAY may suggest heat from radioactivity, but it is not a heat-transfer term; BOND, REACT and ADAPT are also verbs.
